## SECTION | DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS
### The Painting
Masterworks agreed to acquire Hammer 5 (2010) at Christie’s evening sale of Post-War and Contemporary Art in London for £800,625 ($989,723) on October 4, 2019, though closing of the sale will occur on the earlier of (i) closing of this Offering and (ii) January 2, 2020. In this work, Jonas Wood revisits his ‘New Plant’ series through the lens of his first solo institutional exhibition at the Hammer Museum in Los Angeles in 2010. The monumental canvas, 90 in, x 114 in., abstracts and flattens a view of two walls on which three of the ‘New Plants’ hang.
On October 4, 2019, prior to the auction at which Masterworks agreed to purchase the Painting, the closing of the sale of which has yet to occur, the Painting was appraised at $1,800,000. The appraisal, a copy of which is attached as an exhibit to the Intercompany Agreement which is filed as Exhibit 6.2 to the offering statement of which this offering circular is an integral part, is relevant only as of the date it was issued and is subject to important qualifications and limitations as set forth therein. Although, the Company believes the pre-auction appraisal provides relevant information for investors, it should only be viewed as a statement of opinion, and, undue emphasis should not be placed on the appraisal amount. Valuation of unique art objects requires a high degree of subjectivity, so while the Company acknowledges that a sale at a public auction is one of the strongest indicators of value, it is not the only piece of information that should be taken into account. Unlike an auction for homogenous commodities with a deep demand base, the market for fine art is far more idiosyncratic and inefficient. The Company believes that it is typical for a buyer to overpay or underpay for an item at auction relative to its fair market value depending on a variety of factors, where a single event can have a significant impact on supply and demand. This is the case because the art market is characterized by a limited number of potential buyers, particularly for items as valuable as the Painting. Therefore, the singularity of each item, the timing and location of particular sales, and global economic conditions, may all significantly influence the outcome of an auction sale. The appraisal itself contains valuable information for potential investors, including a description of the methodology and specific attributes of the Painting considered by a professional art appraisal company to be meaningful in the determination of fair market value. Notwithstanding the foregoing, investors should not place undue emphasis on the appraised value.

## SECTION | DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS
### The Artist
The discussions contained in this offering circular relating to Jonas Wood, the Painting and the art industry are taken from third-party sources that the Company believes to be reliable and the Company believes that the information from such sources contained herein regarding Jonas Wood, the Painting and the art industry is reasonable, and that the factual information therein is fair and accurate.
Jonas Wood (b. 1977, Boston) is one of the most important ultra-contemporary artists working today. His work first appeared at auction in 2011 with total sales below $100,000 annually until his auction market grew to $4.9 million in 2015 (excluding works on paper, editions and prints) when his large-scale canvases first became available. In 2019 year-to-date, Wood’s average realized sales price at auction was approximately $959,000 and has increased at a 40% compound annual growth rate since 2015. The rising prices and volume speak to the breadth of Woods’ collector base and appeal, which include several prominent art collectors, including Eli Broad, Yusaku Maezawa, and Maurice and Paul Marciano.
The artist, who recently had his first major museum survey of his work at the Dallas Museum of Art, is continuing to see momentum build for his market. His auction record, set with the painting Japanese Garden 3, achieved a realized sale price of $4.9 million at Christie’s in May 2019 and was approximately double his prior record. Auction sales for the artist’s work have already exceeded $21 million in 2019 year-to-date and have increased at a 46% compound annual growth rate since 2015. This September, Wood was invited to collaborate with fashion powerhouse Louis Vuitton, following in the footsteps of superstar artists like Jeff Koons and Yayoi Kusama.

## SECTION | DETERMINATION OF OFFERING PRICE
The price per each Class A share was determined by dividing (1) the sum of (a) purchase price that Masterworks paid for the Painting, $989,723, plus (b) approximately 10.00% of such amount, or $99,277 as a true-up payable to Masterworks, by (2) 54,450, which is the maximum number of Class A shares that will be sold in this Offering (or issued to Masterworks if any remain unsold). Masterworks Gallery will own 13,613 Class B shares representing a 20% profits interest in our Company following the Offering and will own Class A shares if and to the extent the Offering is not fully subscribed, since the number of unsold Class A shares, if any, will be paid to Masterworks to repay the advance made by Masterworks to acquire the Painting and to pay the true-up. Prior to this Offering, no public market exists for the Class A shares, and there can be no assurance that a public market will ever exist for the Class A shares. The Company believes that based on the price paid for the Painting at public auction, historical appreciation rates of similar paintings by the same artist and other factors, the per share offering price constitutes a reasonable estimate of the fair value of the Class A shares as of the date of this Offering Circular.

## SECTION | SUMMARY
### Overview
We were formed as a Delaware limited liability company on October 7, 2019 to facilitate an investment in the Painting. Masterworks will manage all maintenance and administrative services relating to the Painting and the Company. We will not conduct any business activities except for activities relating to an investment in, maintenance, promotion and the eventual sale of the Painting. Our strategy will be to display and promote the Painting so as to enhance its value and broaden its exposure to the art-viewing public.
Masterworks agreed to purchase the Painting at Christie’s evening sale of Post-War and Contemporary Art on October 4, 2019 for $989,723 (£800,625). We are offering 54,450 Class A shares in this Regulation A+ Offering for an aggregate subscription amount of $1,089,000.
We do not expect to generate any revenues or cash flow unless and until the Painting is sold and no profits will be realized by investors unless they are able to sell their Class A shares or the Painting is sold. We will be totally reliant on Masterworks for administrative services and to fund operations.
